name: ARoS
funding: Aarhus Municipality, Salling Fonden, Ny Carlsbergfondet and many foundations. Augustinus Fonden backed several 2025 shows and gave grants of DKK 2M for 2026 projects.
watch: Major Danish art museum topped by Olafur Eliasson's 'Your rainbow panorama'.
why_flagged: Aarhus Municipality, Salling Fonden, Ny Carlsbergfondet and many foundations. Augustinus Fonden backed several 2025 shows and gave grants of DKK 2M for 2026 projects.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2010 to 2025 with audited accounts, a named board and a 2025 list of sponsors and foundations.

name: Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam
funding: €37.5M income (2024), City of Amsterdam 62%. VriendenLoterij is main partner; IMC, ABN AMRO, Mastercard, Polestar and Teijin are loyal partners; Ammodo and the Mondriaan Fund also give.
watch: ABN AMRO is a loyal partner (2024 report). It paid €480M in 2021 to settle a Dutch money-laundering case covering 2014 to 2020.
records_note: The Stedelijk's 2024 report summary, on its own file host, names partners and gives a financial overview with an auditor's opinion; its website blocked checks.

name: Fondation Vincent van Gogh Arles
funding: Set up in 2010 after Luc Hoffmann backed it. Maja Hoffmann, a Roche heir, chairs the board, which includes the Mayor of Arles. Partners: Hiscox, Blackwall Green, Christie's.
watch: Roche is a pharmaceutical group, no flag category. Maja Hoffmann also chairs the LUMA Foundation behind LUMA Arles.
records_note: Names its institutional partners, corporate partners and sponsors on a partners page and lists its board of directors; no annual reports or accounts are posted.

name: Luma Arles
funding: Funded by the LUMA Foundation of Maja Hoffmann, a Roche heir. Artnet put the total project cost at about EUR 150M.
records_note: States that it was created and funded by the LUMA Foundation of Maja Hoffmann, and publishes no reports, accounts, donor list or board.

name: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki
funding: 497,998 visitors (2024-25). Run by Tātaki Auckland Unlimited for Auckland Council. Partners include BMW, Van Cleef & Arpels, HSBC, Anthony Harper, Baker Tilly; trusts include Chartwell and Mackelvie.
watch: HSBC backed A Century of Modern Art in 2025. HSBC agreed a $1.92 billion US penalty in December 2012 over money-laundering failures.
records_note: Parent Tataki Auckland Unlimited posts audited annual reports 2021 to 2026 and its board; the gallery's own 2024-25 review names partners and trusts.

name: MACBA (Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona)
funding: €13.2M budget. Consortium comprising the Generalitat de Catalunya, Ajuntament de Barcelona, Spanish Ministry of Culture, and Fundació MACBA.
watch: Repsol is a fossil-fuel funder; Naturgy executives on the board.
why_flagged: Repsol is a fossil-fuel funder; Naturgy executives on the board.
records_note: MACBA posts its 2025 general accounts and audit reports for 2011 to 2018 and names its trustees, but no annual report or donor list.

name: The Bowes Museum
funding: £3.9M income (FY2025). Arts Council England, Durham County Council, National Lottery Heritage Fund £250k, Wolfson Foundation, Swire Charitable Trust, Art Fund, about 20 other trusts; Darlington Building Society, Global Radio.
watch: Arms and Armour Heritage Trust is a heritage charity, not an arms maker. No flagged funder or protest found.
records_note: No annual report on its site; accounts 2021 to 2025 are on the Charity Commission register, a supporters page names donors, trustees are listed.

name: Kunsthalle Basel
funding: Canton Basel-Stadt CHF 950k a year for 2024-27 (32% of budget); third-party grants about CHF 660k (30%); restaurant and property rent 22%; members 8%.
watch: In November 2023 an SVP member of the cantonal parliament demanded subsidy be cut over director Almusibli's ceasefire letters; the canton did not act.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2014 to 2025 with financial statements, names members and corporate supporters in the 2025 report, and lists its association board.

name: Kunstmuseum Basel
funding: Canton Basel-Stadt and the Emanuel Hoffmann, Christoph Merian and Laurenz foundations. UBS is partner; Novartis, KPMG, Trafina and the Federal Office of Culture are sponsors.
watch: UBS paid a $100M Federal Reserve fine in 2004 over dollar dealings with sanctioned states. Novartis paid $678M in 2020 over kickbacks to doctors.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2010 to 2025 with accounts, names its partner and sponsors undated, and lists its Board of Trustees.

name: Museum Tinguely
funding: Roche has paid all operating costs since the museum opened in 1996 as a gift for its centenary; Roche built it and funds collection additions.
watch: Roche pleaded guilty in 1999 to a worldwide vitamin price-fixing conspiracy and paid $500M in US criminal fines.
records_note: The museum has no records of its own; funder Roche posts annual and finance reports 2020 to 2025 and its board; no donor list.

name: Schaulager
funding: Made possible by the Laurenz Foundation, founded in 1999 by Maja Oeri and Hans U. Bodenmann. The foundation does not give grants; no other funders are named.
watch: Herzog & de Meuron built it in 2002-03. The Emanuel Hoffmann Foundation collection is its core.
records_note: It posts no reports, accounts or donors; its Laurenz Foundation pages name the foundation board and say the foundation makes Schaulager possible.

name: Dia Beacon
funding: Dia Art Foundation endowment, Andrew W. Mellon Foundation, individual board patrons.
watch: Dropped the Sackler name 2019; Schlumberger origin.
